full_judgment:
"That the suit the decreed exparte with costs. The right title and interest of the plaintiff over the suit land be decreed and they do get khas possession in respect of the same by evicting the defendants therefrom and removing all obstacles. The defendants are however, permitted to remove their structures upon suit land within 30 days of the decree failing which the plaintiffs will be at liberty to get the structures removed by putting the decree into execution." 

 6. On behalf of the petitioners it is urged by Mr. Fazlul Karim the learned Advocate that the decree sought to be executed being one for khas possession by evicting the judgment-debtors from the decretal land after removing all obstacles and structures standing thereon, it was the duty of the court to execute the same in terms thereof and in the manner provided by Order 21 Rule 35 of the Code according to which the actual possession or the land ought to have been delivered to the decree-holders and since the decree-holders had been delivered symbolical possession instead of actual possession to which they were entitled under the decree, it is not only proper but incumbent for the court to order for fresh delivery of possession in the facts of the case. The learned Advocate, therefore, maintains that the court of appeal below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in dismissing the execution case as being not maintainable. 

 7. In reply Mr. S. R. Pal, the learned Advocate who appears for the judgment-debtors-opposite-parties contends that the decree-holders accepted delivery of symbolical possession without removal of the persons in possession and of the structures standing on the decretal land and so they cannot now proceed with the execution for khas possession. According to him the decree-holders by their own conduct have disentitled themselves to the remedy they now ask for and the only remedy now lying open to them is to go for a suit. 

 11. In the said Calcutta case, in execution of a decree for khas possession after demolition of the structure a writ under Order 21 Rule 35 of the Code was issued. The peon delivered possession to the agent of the decree-holder by fixing up a bamboo accompanied with beating of drum. On the returnable date the decree-holder appeared in the court to put in talabana for issue of notice as regards the execution of the decree for costs, but raised no objection of his not having khas possession in accordance with the terms of the writ and the court recorded an order "possession delivered on the decretal land". Subsequently the decree-holder made second application for execution praying khas possession. A question, therefore, arose whether a fresh execution was permissible in the said circumstances. The question was answered in the negative. Mukerjee, J. who delivered the judgment for a Division Bench expressed himself in the following language:" 

 The case, therefore, seems to me be one of those cases in which a decree-holder having armed himself with a decree for khas possession executes that decree in the first instance by obtaining symbolical possession only with some ulterior object of his own and thereafter subsequently and as a second installment asks for khas possession. The question is whether such a course is permissible under the law. I am of opinion that it is not." 

 "If in the present case the conduct of the decree-holder might be construed as indicating a repudiation on his part of the symbolical possession which the peon had given him or at least as disclosing desire on his part not to be content at the time with the kind of possession that the peon had given him but to get the khas possession which he was entitled to under the decree and for which he had prayed in his first application for execution, I should be prepared to hold that he was perfectly within his rights to come before the executing Court to have his remedy."
